name: xccdf-org.cisecurity.benchmarks-benchmark-1.2.0-cis-google-chrome-benchmark

descriptions.data: Allows access to local files on the machine by allowing Google Chrome to display file selection dialogs.
descriptions.label: default

descriptions.data:
To establish the recommended configuration via Group Policy, set the following UI path to Enabled.
                     Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Classic Administrative Template (ADM)\Google\Google Chrome\Allow invocation of file selection dialogs 
                     Impact:
                     
                        If you enable this setting, users can open file selection dialogs as normal.
descriptions.label: fix

descriptions.data: Preventing users from uploading documents can help limit the loss of sensitive information.
descriptions.label: rationale

requirements.title: (L2) Ensure 'Allow invocation of file selection dialogs' is set to 'Enabled'

descriptions.data: Chrome enables the use of outdated plugins. By disabling this feature Chrome will not prompt the user to use an outdated plugin.
descriptions.label: default

descriptions.data:
To establish the recommended configuration via Group Policy, set the following UI path to Disabled.
                     Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Classic Administrative Template (ADM)\Google\Google Chrome\Allow running plugins that are outdated 
                     Impact:
                     
                        If you disable this setting, outdated plugins will not be used and users will not be asked for permission to run them.
descriptions.label: fix

descriptions.data: Running the most up-to-date version of a plugin can reduce the possibility of running a plugin that contains an exploit or security hole.
descriptions.label: rationale

requirements.title: (L1) Ensure 'Allow running plugins that are outdated' is set to 'Disabled'

descriptions.data: Chrome allows plugins that are not outdated to run automatically. Disabling this setting allows the plugins to run only when permission is granted by the user.
descriptions.label: default

descriptions.data:
To establish the recommended configuration via Group Policy, set the following UI path to Disabled.
                     Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Classic Administrative Template (ADM)\Google\Google Chrome\Always runs plugins that require authorization 
                     Impact:
                     
                        If this setting is disabled or not set, users will be asked for permission to run plugins that require authorization. These are plugins that can potentially compromise security.
descriptions.label: fix

descriptions.data: Disabling plugins from automatically running can prevent unwanted and/or harmful plugins from running without the user’s consent, limiting unauthorized data/remote access.
descriptions.label: rationale

requirements.title: (L1) Ensure 'Always runs plugins that require authorization' is set to 'Disabled'

descriptions.data: Chrome allows cookies to be set by web page elements that are not from the domain in the user's address bar. Enabling this feature prevents third party cookies from being set.
descriptions.label: default

descriptions.data:
To establish the recommended configuration via Group Policy, set the following UI path to Enabled.
                     Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Classic Administrative Template (ADM)\Google\Google Chrome\Block third party cookies 
                     Impact:
                     
                        Enabling this setting prevents cookies from being set by web page elements that are not from the domain that is in the browser's address bar.
descriptions.label: fix

descriptions.data: Blocking third party cookies can help protect a user's privacy by eliminating a number of website tracking cookies.
descriptions.label: rationale

requirements.title: (L1) Ensure 'Block third party cookies' is set to 'Enabled'

descriptions.data: Chrome allows for processes started while the browser is open to remain running once the browser has been closed. It also allows for background apps and the current browsing session to remain active after the browser has been closed. Disabling this feature will stop all processes and background applications when the browser window is closed.
descriptions.label: default

descriptions.data:
To establish the recommended configuration via Group Policy, set the following UI path to Disabled.
                     Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Classic Administrative Template (ADM)\Google\Google Chrome\Continue running background apps when Google Chrome is closed 
                     Impact:
                     
                        If this policy is set to Disabled, background mode is disabled and cannot be controlled by the user in the browser settings.
descriptions.label: fix

descriptions.data: If this setting is enabled, vulnerable or malicious plugins, apps and processes can continue running even after Chrome has closed.
descriptions.label: rationale

requirements.title: (L1) Ensure 'Continue running background apps when Google Chrome is closed' is set to 'Disabled'

descriptions.data: Chrome allows users to auto-complete web forms with saved information such as address, phone number and credit card numbers. Disabling this feature will prompt a user to enter all information manually.
descriptions.label: default

descriptions.data:
To establish the recommended configuration via Group Policy, set the following UI path to Disabled.
                     Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Classic Administrative Template (ADM)\Google\Google Chrome\Enable AutoFill 
                     Impact:
                     
                        If this setting is disabled, AutoFill will be inaccessible to users.
descriptions.label: fix

descriptions.data: If an attacker gains access to a user's machine where the user has stored auto save data, information could be harvested or used to gain access to more systems.
descriptions.label: rationale

descriptions.data: This setting enables Google Chrome to act as a proxy between Google Cloud Print and legacy printers connected to the machine.
descriptions.label: default

descriptions.data:
To establish the recommended configuration via Group Policy, set the following UI path to Disabled.
                     Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Classic Administrative Template (ADM)\Google\Google Chrome\Enable Google Cloud Print Proxy 
                     Impact:
                     
                        If this setting is disabled, users cannot enable the proxy, and the machine will not be allowed to share its local printers with Google Cloud Print.
descriptions.label: fix

descriptions.data: Disabling this option will prevent users from printing possible confidential enterprise documents through the cloud.
descriptions.label: rationale

requirements.title: (L1) Ensure 'Enable Google Cloud Print Proxy' is set to 'Disabled'

descriptions.data: This Setting controls anonymous reporting of usage and crash-related data about Google Chrome to Google.
descriptions.label: default

descriptions.data:
To establish the recommended configuration via Group Policy, set the following UI path to Disabled.
                     Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Classic Administrative Template (ADM)\Google\Google Chrome\Enable reporting of usage and crash-related data 
                     Impact:
                     
                        If this setting is disabled, this information is not sent to Google.
descriptions.label: fix

descriptions.data: Anonymous crash/usage data can be used to identify people, companies and information, which can be considered data ex-filtration from company systems.
descriptions.label: rationale

requirements.title: (L1) Ensure 'Enable reporting of usage and crash-related data' is set to 'Disabled'

descriptions.data: This setting enables Google Chrome to submit documents to Google Cloud Print for printing. NOTE: This only affects Google Cloud Print support in Google Chrome. It does not prevent users from submitting print jobs on web sites.
descriptions.label: default

descriptions.data:
To establish the recommended configuration via Group Policy, set the following UI path to Disabled.
                     Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Classic Administrative Template (ADM)\Google\Google Chrome\Enable submission of documents to Google Cloud print 
                     Impact:
                     
                        If this setting is disabled, users cannot print to Google Cloud Print from the Chrome print dialog
descriptions.label: fix

descriptions.data: Disabling this option will prevent users from printing possible confidential enterprise documents through the cloud.
descriptions.label: rationale

requirements.title: (L1) Ensure 'Enable submission of documents to Google Cloud print' is set to 'Disabled'

descriptions.data: This setting controls if saved passwords from the default browser can be imported.
descriptions.label: default

descriptions.data:
To establish the recommended configuration via Group Policy, set the following UI path to Disabled.
                     Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Classic Administrative Template (ADM)\Google\Google Chrome\Import saved passwords from default browser on first run 
                     Impact:
                     
                        If this setting is disabled, saved passwords from other browsers are not imported.
descriptions.label: fix

descriptions.data: In Chrome, passwords can be stored in plain-text and revealed by clicking the “show” button next to the password field by going to chrome://settings/passwords/.
descriptions.label: rationale

requirements.title: (L1) Ensure 'Import saved passwords from default browser on first run' is set to 'Disabled'

descriptions.data: Chrome allows for the automatic search and installation of missing plugins. Disabling this feature will stop plugins from being downloaded and installed without the user's consent or knowledge.
descriptions.label: default

descriptions.data:
To establish the recommended configuration via Group Policy, set the following UI path to Enabled.
                     Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Classic Administrative Template (ADM)\Google\Google Chrome\Specify whether the plugin finder should be disabled 
                     Impact:
                     
                        If this settings is enabled, the automatic search and installation of missing plugins will be disabled in Google Chrome.
descriptions.label: fix

descriptions.data: Disabling the feature that allows plugins to automatically be installed prevents plugins that may have vulnerabilities or be against company policy from being introduced to the computer without anyone’s knowledge.
descriptions.label: rationale

requirements.title: (L1) Ensure 'Specify whether the plugin finder should be disabled' is set to 'Enabled'

descriptions.data: Chrome allows the user to configure a required host domain that is imposed on remote access hosts. When enabled, hosts can only be shared using accounts that are registered to the specified domain.
descriptions.label: default

descriptions.data:
To establish the recommended configuration via Group Policy, set the following UI path to Enabled and enter domain.
                     Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Classic Administative Templates (ADM)\Google\Google Chrome\Configure remote access options\Configure the required domain name for remote access hosts 
                     Impact:
                     
                        If this setting is enabled, hosts can be shared only using accounts registered on the specified domain name.
descriptions.label: fix

descriptions.data: If this setting is disabled or not set, then hosts can be shared using any account.
descriptions.label: rationale

requirements.title: (L1) Ensure 'Configure the required domain name for remote access hosts' is set to 'Enabled'

descriptions.data: Chrome allows the user to disable a remote user's physical input and output while the remote connection is in progress.
descriptions.label: default

descriptions.data:
To establish the recommended configuration via Group Policy, set the following UI path to Enabled.
                     Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Classic Administative Templates (ADM)\Google\Google Chrome\Configure remote access options\Enable curtaining of remote access hosts 
                     Impact:
                     
                        If this setting is enabled, host's physical input and output devices are disabled while a remote connection is in progress.
descriptions.label: fix

descriptions.data: If this setting is disabled or not set, then both local and remote users can interact with the host when it is being shared.
descriptions.label: rationale

requirements.title: (L1) Ensure 'Enable curtaining of remote access hosts' is set to 'Enabled'

descriptions.data: Chrome enables the usage of STUN servers which allows remote clients to discover and connect to a machine even if they are separated by a firewall. By disabling this feature, in conjunction with filtering outgoing UDP connections, the machine will only allow connections from machines within the local network.
descriptions.label: default

descriptions.data:
To establish the recommended configuration via Group Policy, set the following UI path to Disabled.
                      Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Classic Administrative Template (ADM)\Google\Google Chrome\Configure remote access options\Enable firewall traversal from remote access host 
                     Impact:
                     
                        If this setting is disabled and outgoing UDP connections are filtered by the firewall, this machine will only allow connections from client machines within the local network.
descriptions.label: fix

descriptions.data: If this setting is enabled, remote clients can discover and connect to this machines even if they are separated by a firewall.
descriptions.label: rationale

requirements.title: (L1) Ensure 'Enable firewall traversal from remote access host' is set to 'Disabled'

descriptions.data: Chrome enables a user to opt-out of using user-specified PIN authentication and instead pair clients and hosts during connection time.
descriptions.label: default

descriptions.data:
To establish the recommended configuration via Group Policy, set the following UI path to ``Disabled.
                     
                     Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Classic Administative Templates (ADM)\Google\Google Chrome\Configure remote access options\Enable or disable PIN-less authentication 
                     Impact:
                     
                        If this setting is disabled, users will be required to enter PIN every time.
descriptions.label: fix

descriptions.data: If this setting is enabled or not configured, users can opt to pair clients and hosts at connection time, eliminating the need to enter a PIN every time.
descriptions.label: rationale

requirements.title: (L1) Ensure 'Enable or disable PIN-less authentication for remote access hosts' is set to 'Disabled'

descriptions.data: Allows you to set whether websites are allowed to set local data. Setting local data can be either allowed for all websites or denied for all websites.
descriptions.label: default

descriptions.data:
To establish the recommended configuration via Group Policy, set the following UI path to Enabled.
                     Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Classic Administrative Template (ADM)\Google\Google Chrome\Content Settings\Default cookies setting 
                     Impact:
                     
                        If this setting is enabled, cookies will be cleared when the session closes.
descriptions.label: fix

descriptions.data: If this policy is left not set, 'AllowCookies' will be used and the user will be able to change it.
descriptions.label: rationale

requirements.title: (L2) Ensure 'Default cookies setting' is set to 'Enabled' (Keep cookies for the duration of the session)

descriptions.data: Allows you to set whether websites are allowed to automatically run plugins. Automatically running plugins can be either allowed for all websites or denied for all websites.
descriptions.label: default

descriptions.data:
To establish the recommended configuration via Group Policy, set the following UI path to Enabledwith click to play selected from the drop down.
                     Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Classic Administrative Template (ADM)\Google\Google Chrome\Content Settings\Default Plugins Setting 
                     Impact:
                     
                        If this setting is enabled, users must click plugins to allow their execution
descriptions.label: fix

descriptions.data: Malicious plugins can cause browser instability and erratic behavior so setting the value to click to play will allow a user to only run necessary plugins.
descriptions.label: rationale

requirements.title: (L1) Ensure 'Default Plugin Setting' is set to 'Enabled' (Click to Play)

descriptions.data: Enabling this setting allows you to specify which extensions the users can NOT install. Extensions already installed will be removed if blacklisted.
descriptions.label: default

descriptions.data:
To establish the recommended configuration via Group Policy, set the following UI path to Enabled.
                     Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Classic Administrative Template (ADM)\Google\Google Chrome\Extensions\Configure Extension Installation Blacklist 
                     Impact:
                     
                        Any installed extension will be removed unless it is specified on the extension whitelist.
descriptions.label: fix

descriptions.data: This can be used to block extensions that could potentially allow remote control of the system through the browser. If there are extensions needed for securing the browser or for enterprise use these can be enabled by configuring the extension whitelist.
descriptions.label: rationale

requirements.title: (L1) Ensure 'Configure extension installation blacklist' is set to 'Enabled' ("*" for all extensions)

descriptions.data: Chrome will memorize passwords and automatically provide them when a user logs into a site. By disabling this feature the user will be prompted to enter their password each time they visit a website.
descriptions.label: default

descriptions.data:
To establish the recommended configuration via Group Policy, set the following UI path to Disabled.
                     Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Classic Administrative Template (ADM)\Google\Google Chrome\Password manager\Enable the password manager 
                     Impact:
                     
                        If this setting is disable, users are not able to save passwords or use previously saved passwords.
descriptions.label: fix

descriptions.data: If this setting is enabled, users can have Google Chrome memorize passwords and provide them automatically the next time they log in to a site. An intruder who has unrestricted access to your computer for even a minute can view and copy all of your saved passwords just by visiting an easy-to-remember settings page: chrome://settings/passwords.
descriptions.label: rationale

requirements.title: (L1) Ensure 'Enable the password manager' is set to 'Disabled'

summary: This document provides prescriptive guidance for establishing a secure configuration posture for Google Chrome Browser. This guide was tested against Google Chrome v59.0.3071.86. To obtain the latest version of this guide, please visit http://benchmarks.cisecurity.org. If you have questions, comments, or have identified ways to improve this guide, please write us at feedback@cisecurity.org.
